title: Cricket Australia Opens Door to Hosting IPL Matches in Landmark Exchange With BCCI
excerpt: Following the announcement that the BBL season opener will be played in Chennai, Cricket Australia has initiated discussions with the BCCI about bringing IPL fixtures to Australian venues as early as March 2027.
body:
• Cricket Australia has opened discussions with the BCCI about hosting IPL matches in Australia, with Adelaide Oval positioning itself as the frontrunner venue for a potential fixture as early as March 2027
  • The talks follow the announcement that the 2026-27 BBL season opener will be staged in Chennai on December 12 — the first time the Big Bash League has been played outside Australia
  • The proposal is part of a broader Sports Cooperation Roadmap announced during PM Modi's visit to Australia, signalling deeper bilateral cricketing ties
  • An IPL match in Australia would be the first overseas fixture driven by commercial strategy rather than security or pandemic necessity

Cricket Australia has initiated discussions with the Board of Control for Cricket in India about hosting Indian Premier League matches on Australian soil, according to a report by the Sydney Morning Herald. The proposal remains at an exploratory stage, but it represents the most concrete step yet toward taking the world's richest T20 league outside India for strategic rather than emergency reasons.

The conversations follow a landmark announcement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Australia: the Melbourne Renegades will face the Perth Scorchers in the opening match of the 2026-27 Big Bash League season at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on December 12, 2026. It will be the first time Australia's premier T20 competition has been played outside the country.

Adelaide Leads the Charge

While no specific IPL match has been confirmed, Adelaide Oval has emerged as the most proactive contender. According to SEN Cricket, South Australian Cricket Association (SACA) president Will Rayner and Adelaide Oval chairman Jamie Briggs have held preliminary discussions with multiple stakeholders about bringing an IPL fixture to the venue in March 2027.

March aligns with the start of the IPL season, which typically runs from March to May. Adelaide Oval officials have pointed to the venue's capacity of 53,500, its status as host of the 2028 T20 World Cup final, and their ability to transition the ground from cricket to Australian rules football within 48 hours as evidence of logistical readiness.

Other venues under consideration include the Melbourne Cricket Ground, Sydney Cricket Ground and Perth Stadium, all identified by Cricket Australia as potential hosts.

A Strategic Shift, Not an Emergency

The IPL has been played outside India before, but always out of necessity. The entire 2009 season was held in South Africa because of security concerns during India's general elections. The first half of the 2014 tournament moved to the UAE for similar reasons, and the second half of the 2021 season was shifted to the Emirates because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

An Australian fixture would mark the first time the IPL has been taken abroad primarily for commercial and strategic purposes. Cricket Australia views it as an opportunity to engage Australia's large and growing Indian diaspora while showcasing the country's cricket infrastructure.

"If big teams like the Chennai Super Kings or Royal Challengers Bengaluru, or big names like Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, or MS Dhoni, arrive in Adelaide, you can expect a wild atmosphere."

— SEN Cricket report on Adelaide Oval's pitch to host IPL

The Broader Partnership

The BBL-in-Chennai and IPL-in-Australia discussions sit within a larger India-Australia Sports Cooperation Roadmap announced by the two prime ministers. Officials on both sides are exploring how regular domestic cricket exchanges could create a more integrated relationship beyond traditional bilateral series and broadcast deals.

Broadcast experts believe the cross-pollination could increase the BBL's footprint in India's massive cricket market while amplifying the IPL's popularity among Australian fans. Some officials are hopeful the success of domestic crossovers could even revive the Champions League T20, the franchise tournament that was discontinued after struggling to attract audiences despite launching in 2008.

Hurdles Ahead

Any proposal to stage IPL matches abroad requires approval from the BCCI, IPL franchise owners, broadcasters and commercial partners. Scheduling presents challenges given the tournament's packed calendar, player availability and broadcast commitments. Industry observers believe any overseas matches, if approved, are more likely to involve a limited number of fixtures rather than a full relocation.

For Australia's estimated 800,000-strong Indian diaspora, the prospect of watching the IPL live on home soil carries particular excitement. Tourism South Australia is already supportive of the idea, recognising the economic impact thousands of visiting fans could bring to Adelaide and beyond.
nri_angle: Australia's estimated 800,000-strong Indian diaspora could see IPL matches played on their doorstep, as Cricket Australia courts the BCCI with a venue exchange.
